title: Bed and property history: who has occupied this space, and when
description:
User request, the other half of LODGY-92: opening a bed should show which tenants have lived in it, and the same for a shop, warehouse or flat.

BLOCKED ON LODGY-91 AND NOT WORTH ATTEMPTING BEFORE IT. Today a tenancy stores only its current bed, so this screen would answer the question wrongly while looking authoritative: on the current data, asking who has occupied Room 101 Bed A returns one tenant when three have lived there. A history view that quietly omits people is worse than no history view, because the warden will believe it.

WHERE IT GOES: the bed sheet already opens on a tap and already carries the room's details and the current occupant (LODGY-69, LODGY-71), so it is the natural home - past occupants below the present one.

WHY A WARDEN WANTS IT: a bed comes back damaged and they need to know who had it and for how long; a tenant claims a fitting was already broken when they arrived; the warden is working out which beds turn over constantly and which are stable, which is a letting decision rather than a record-keeping one.

SHOPS, WAREHOUSES AND FLATS ARE THE SAME QUERY, NOT A SECOND FEATURE. A single-unit property's implicit bed is the unit, so the history is identical underneath - only the wording changes, and LODGY-86 already established the rule: a property let whole is named as itself and never as a bed inside a room inside itself. Getting that wrong here would reintroduce exactly the defect LODGY-86 fixed.

AND THE GAP BETWEEN OCCUPANCIES matters as much as the occupancies. A warden looking at this screen is often asking why a bed keeps sitting empty, so the vacant stretches between tenants are part of the answer, not whitespace.
acceptanceCriteria: A bed shows every tenancy that has occupied it, most recent first, with the dates each covered
A tenant who transferred away from this bed still appears in its history
The current occupant is clearly the current one, not just the newest row in a list
A shop, warehouse or flat shows the same history worded for a whole property - no room number, no bed label
A bed that has never been occupied says so plainly rather than showing an empty list
Vacant stretches between occupancies are visible, since 'why does this keep sitting empty' is a reason to open this screen
Warden and caretaker occupancy appears in the history like any other, since the room was genuinely occupied
Correct in Hindi as well as English

history.note: Filed from a user request alongside LODGY-92. Hard-blocked on LODGY-91: without occupancy periods this screen returns a confidently incomplete answer, which is the one outcome worse than not shipping it.

LODGY-94 has been filed so the warden can enter past stays themselves. It matters to this ticket because without it this screen opens blank for every stay that predates the feature - which for an existing warden is most of them - and the empty state would be the normal case rather than the exception. Worth designing the empty state on the assumption that backfill exists and may or may not have been used.
Starting, on top of LODGY-91's occupancy_periods table (now built, in Testing).

Built: the bed sheet (BedGridScreen's BedActionSheet) now lists past occupants below 'Occupied by X', built live via a new OccupancyPeriodDao.observeByBedId query (BedGridViewModel.onBedSelected/onBedSheetDismissed manage the collection's lifecycle so it doesn't leak across bed taps). Vacant stretches between tenancies are computed by a new pure, tested function (ui/property/BedHistory.kt: bedHistoryEntries walks periods chronologically and turns any gap into its own row; pastOccupancyEntries excludes the still-open period itself but keeps a gap right before it visible). A bed with no periods at all says 'Never occupied.' plainly. No room/bed labels are printed in the rows themselves, so a shop/warehouse/flat's history reads correctly with no code branch needed. Docs: DESIGN.md 4.3 + decision log, USER-MANUAL.md property section. Unit tests: BedHistoryTest (the gap/exclusion logic), BedGridViewModelTest extended (history loads on select, clears on dismiss). FULL SUITE ACROSS LODGY-91/92/93/94 (all four tickets' code together): 630 tests, 0 failures, line coverage 95.71% (gate 0.93), assembleDebug succeeds. Caught and fixed 4 test bugs of my own before this passed (a MockK stub-ordering mistake and three wrong hand-computed expected values) - noting it so the tester knows the suite was actually exercised, not just written. SAME FLAG AS LODGY-91/92/94: not verified on a device - no working emulator this session (see LODGY-91's note for what was tried). SEPARATELY: this session's gradle runs repeatedly got OOM-killed by Windows - the machine has 8GB total RAM and Android Studio alone was holding 1.1-1.4GB with my own orphaned Gradle/Kotlin daemons stacking on top after each kill; had to manually kill leftover java.exe processes between attempts to get a clean run through. Worth the PO/warden knowing this machine is tight for local Android builds alongside Studio.
See LODGY-91's comment at 2026-09-17T15:50:00Z - the device migration verification flagged on all four of LODGY-91/92/93/94 is done, on a populated database, with no data loss and no crash.
